Split.IO

Split.IO feature flags, environments and change requests through the Split Admin API

skills/toil/splitio.md

Feature flags, environments and change requests on Split.IO (Harness FME), through the Admin API under /internal/api/v2. The reads list workspaces, environments, flags and change requests; every write files a change request that Split’s approvers then accept or reject. toil never changes a flag directly. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Split.IO Admin API version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil calls the Admin API under /internal/api/v2 with an Admin API key sent as a Bearer header. It has not been run against a live Split account yet.

Credential

A Split Admin API key: in Split, Admin settings → API keys → Create API key, with the type Admin. toil sends it as Authorization: Bearer <key>. There is no login and no token exchange.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_SPLITIO_BASE_URLyesAdmin API root, normally https://api.split.io
adminApiKeyTOIL_SPLITIO_ADMIN_API_KEYyesAdmin API key
workspaceTOIL_SPLITIO_WORKSPACEnoDefault Split workspace (project) ID, used when --ws is not given

There is no CI fallback variable.

export TOIL_SPLITIO_BASE_URL=https://api.split.io
export TOIL_SPLITIO_ADMIN_API_KEY=<your Admin API key>

Or ~/.toil/config.json:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "split": { "area": "splitio", "baseUrl": "https://api.split.io", "workspace": "<workspace id>" }
  }
}

The key never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add split --area splitio to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_SPLITIO_ADMIN_API_KEY.

The workspace is --ws

Every command but workspaces list and change-requests get acts in one Split workspace: --ws <id>, else the connection’s workspace. Over MCP the field is workspace. On the CLI, --workspace is toil’s own flag for the folder commands may read files in, so --workspace <split id> doesn’t name the Split workspace; a command left without one fails with INVALID_INPUT saying to pass --ws.

Commands

Reads:

  • workspaces list: List all Split.IO workspaces, every page.
  • environments list: List environments in a workspace.
  • flags list: List feature flags in a workspace. --limit (default 50, Split’s maximum) and --offset (default 0); data.totalCount is Split’s total. --flag-set is sent as flagSetName, which Split’s reference doesn’t document, so the result carries a warning to compare totalCount with an unfiltered list.
  • flags get: Get a flag (--flag), or with --environment its definition in that environment: treatments, rules, default rule, kill state.
  • change-requests list: List Change Requests for a workspace (--environment, --status; Split returns REQUESTED ones when --status is unset). --limit defaults to 25 (Split allows 1 to 100). Split pages by marker: pass data.nextMarker (also meta.page.nextCursor) as --after for the next page. --offset accepts only 0, and totalCount is null, since Split reports none.
  • change-requests get: Get a Change Request by ID (--id).

Writes, each a change request against one --environment. They need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write on the call. Every one takes --mnemonic (the title), --description (the comment), --change-number (added to the comment as “Change number: …”, since Split has no field for it), --approvers (comma-separated email addresses, only where the environment lets submitters choose) and --rollout-status <id> (a rollout status ID; Split’s guide says KILL doesn’t need one, and the others may).

  • flags update: Replace a flag’s definition with the JSON object in --input-file (- reads stdin on the CLI). Start from flags get --environment.
  • flags set-rule: Change rule --rule-index (from 0) to one --treatment (a 100% bucket) or --weights (a JSON array of {treatment, size}, sizes in percent; anything but an array is refused). The rest of the definition is copied from the current one.
  • flags set-default: Set the default rule to one --treatment at 100%.
  • flags toggle: --enabled false (or 0) kills the flag; any other value restores it, off and no included. A value other than true or 1 that restores adds a SPLITIO_TOGGLE_RESTORED warning to meta.warnings saying so.
  • flags batch-toggle: One change request per entry of --input-file, a JSON array of {flag, enabled}, titled <mnemonic> — <flag>. A failed entry doesn’t stop the rest; it’s reported in results[] with ok: false, the envelope stays ok, and meta.warnings says how many failed. enabled is read by truthiness, so the string "false" restores. Every entry must have a flag name; if one doesn’t, the command fails with INVALID_INPUT naming the entry, before any request is filed.
  • flags kill, flags restore: Kill or restore a flag in the environment.
  • flags archive: Remove a flag’s definition from the environment (Split’s ARCHIVE change request; not Split’s flag-archive API). CLI only: it removes a definition, and deletes are never served over MCP.
toil splitio workspaces list
toil splitio flags get --ws <workspace id> --flag new_checkout --environment <environment id>
toil splitio flags kill --ws <workspace id> --flag new_checkout --environment <environment id> \
  --mnemonic checkout-off --description "Kill during incident" --change-number CHG0001234 --allow-write

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Admin API root, e.g. https://api.split.io

    TOIL_SPLITIO_BASE_URL

  • adminApiKey required secret

    Split Admin API key

    TOIL_SPLITIO_ADMIN_API_KEY

  • workspace

    Default Split workspace (project) ID, used when --ws is not given

    TOIL_SPLITIO_WORKSPACE

Commands at a glance

  • toil splitioworkspaces list

    List all Split.IO workspaces

    MCP splitio_workspaces_list

  • toil splitioenvironments list

    List environments in a workspace

    MCP splitio_environments_list--ws <id>

  • toil splitioflags list

    List feature flags in a workspace

    MCP splitio_flags_list--limit <n>--offset <n>--flag-set <name>--ws <id>

  • toil splitioflags get

    Get a flag definition

    MCP splitio_flags_get--flag <name>--environment <id>--ws <id>

  • toil splitioflags updatewrite

    Submit a Change Request to replace a flag's full definition in an environment

    MCP splitio_flags_update--flag <name>--environment <id>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--input-file <path>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags set-rulewrite

    Change one targeting rule without altering the rest of the flag definition

    MCP splitio_flags_set_rule--flag <name>--environment <id>--rule-index <n>--treatment <name>--weights <json>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags set-defaultwrite

    Update the fallback default rule for traffic matching no targeting rule

    MCP splitio_flags_set_default--flag <name>--environment <id>--treatment <name>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags togglewrite

    Enable or disable a single flag via a Change Request

    MCP splitio_flags_toggle--flag <name>--environment <id>--enabled <bool>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags batch-togglewrite

    Enable or disable multiple flags from a JSON file (each creates its own Change Request)

    MCP splitio_flags_batch_toggle--environment <id>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--input-file <path>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags killwrite

    Submit a Change Request to kill (disable) a flag

    MCP splitio_flags_kill--flag <name>--environment <id>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags restorewrite

    Submit a Change Request to restore a killed flag

    MCP splitio_flags_restore--flag <name>--environment <id>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitioflags archivewriteCLI only

    Submit a Change Request to remove a flag's definition from an environment

    --flag <name>--environment <id>--mnemonic <text>--description <text>--change-number <CHG>--approvers <ids>--rollout-status <id>--ws <id>--allow-write

  • toil splitiochange-requests list

    List Change Requests for a workspace

    MCP splitio_change_requests_list--environment <id>--status <status>--limit <n>--offset <n>--after <marker>--ws <id>

  • toil splitiochange-requests get

    Get a Change Request by ID

    MCP splitio_change_requests_get--id <id>
